name: Clinical Diagnosis of Urinary Tract Infection in Women (Bent)
condition: Painful or frequent urination (possible bladder infection)

citations.text: Bent S, Nallamothu BK, Simel DL, Fihn SD, Saint S. Does this woman have an acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection? JAMA. 2002;287(20):2701-2710.

validated_population: Adult women with symptoms of acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (systematic review).
license_note: Published diagnostic criteria from a systematic review; not a copyrighted instrument. Question wording is original to OLA BOT.

red_flags.question: Are you vomiting and unable to keep fluids down?
red_flags.help: Being unable to keep fluids down needs same-day care.

items.question: What was your sex assigned at birth?
items.help: This rule was studied in women. Urinary infections in men are handled differently.

items.question: Are you pregnant or could you be pregnant?
items.help: Urinary infections in pregnancy need prompt treatment.

items.question: Do you have a fever (100.4°F / 38°C or higher), chills, or pain in your side or back?
items.help: These can mean the infection has reached the kidney.

items.question: Does it burn or hurt when you urinate?
items.help: Pain or burning while passing urine.

items.question: Do you need to urinate much more often than usual?
items.help: Going to the bathroom much more often, often passing small amounts.

items.question: Have you seen blood in your urine?
Do you have new or unusual vaginal discharge?
items.help: A change in amount, color, or smell.

items.question: Do you have vaginal itching or irritation?
items.help: Itching, soreness, or irritation of the vagina or vulva.

scoring.threshold_text: Painful urination plus frequency, without vaginal discharge or irritation: UTI probability above 90% (Bent 2002). Discharge or irritation lowers the probability and suggests other causes. One urinary symptom alone: probability about 50%.

steps.label: Painful urination AND frequency, without discharge or irritation
At least one urinary symptom (pain, frequency, or blood)

overrides.label: Male (rule not validated; infection is considered complicated)
Fever, chills, or side/back pain (possible kidney infection)

high.label: UTI very likely
high.interpretation: Painful urination plus frequency, without vaginal symptoms, means a bladder infection is very likely (above 90% in the studies reviewed).
high.recommendation: Treatment is usually started based on symptoms. A telehealth or in-person visit can prescribe it.

care.where_detail: Telehealth visit (many insurers cover this; see the number on your insurance card) or an urgent care clinic.
ed_redirect: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Fever with shaking chills or confusion
Severe side or back pain
self_care: Phenazopyridine (over the counter) can ease burning for up to 2 days; it turns urine orange.

intermediate.label: UTI possible
intermediate.interpretation: With one urinary symptom, the chance of a bladder infection is about 50%. A urine test helps decide.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic or primary care clinic that can test urine on site.
ed_redirect: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Fever with shaking chills or confusion
Severe side or back pain

other_cause.label: Other cause possible
other_cause.interpretation: Vaginal discharge or irritation makes a bladder infection less likely and suggests a vaginal infection or sexually transmitted infection.

care.where_detail: Primary care, gynecology, or urgent care clinic that performs pelvic exams.
ed_redirect: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Fever with shaking chills or confusion
Severe side or back pain

unlikely.label: UTI unlikely
unlikely.interpretation: You did not report the main urinary infection symptoms.
unlikely.recommendation: No UTI treatment needed based on these answers.

care.within: Self-care; primary care if symptoms develop
care.where_detail: Home care. Book a primary care visit if new urinary symptoms appear.
ed_redirect: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Fever with shaking chills or confusion
Severe side or back pain

kidney.label: Possible kidney infection
kidney.interpretation: Fever, chills, or side/back pain with urinary symptoms can mean a kidney infection, which needs prompt treatment.
kidney.recommendation: Get an exam and urine test today.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic, or emergency department if you feel very unwell.
ed_redirect: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Fever with shaking chills or confusion
Severe side or back pain

pregnant.label: Pregnancy: needs same-day evaluation
pregnant.interpretation: Urinary infections in pregnancy can affect the pregnancy and need testing and treatment. The Bent criteria were not designed for pregnancy.
pregnant.recommendation: Contact your prenatal care clinic today or go to urgent care.

care.where_detail: Your obstetric (prenatal) clinic's same-day line, or urgent care.
ed_redirect: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Fever with shaking chills or confusion
Severe side or back pain
Bleeding, cramping, or fluid leaking: go to labor and delivery or the emergency department

male.label: Rule does not apply (male)
male.interpretation: The Bent criteria were studied in women. In men, urinary infection is considered complicated and needs an exam and urine test.
male.recommendation: Get an exam and urine test.

care.where_detail: Urgent care or primary care clinic.
ed_redirect: Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
Fever with shaking chills or confusion
Severe side or back pain
Cannot pass urine at all: go to the emergency department
